findings.problem: TelemetryWorkflow uses status:String, is_validated:bool, is_sent:bool, and sent_at_epoch_ms:Option<u64> as independent fields instead of a single typestate enum. This allows illegal state combinations like status='sent' with is_sent=false, or is_validated=true with is_sent=false.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct or mutate TelemetryWorkflow into logically impossible states (e.g., validated but not sent, sent but status still 'pending', sent_at_epoch_ms set without is_sent), violating make-illegal-states-unrepresentable.
findings.fix: Replace all four fields with a single TelemetryState enum with variants like Pending, Validated { validated_at: u64 }, Sent { sent_at: u64 }. Remove is_validated, is_sent, and sent_at_epoch_ms as top-level fields.

findings.problem: status field is String, allowing any arbitrary string value (e.g., 'SENT', 'sent', 'Sent', '', 'deleted', 'cancelled'). mark_sent sets item.status = "sent".to_string() (line 10) which is a mutable string mutation rather than a typed state transition.
findings.failure_mode: Runtime logic branches on string equality against known values; typos produce silent bugs ("sent" vs "SENT"); no compile-time guarantee that status matches lifecycle booleans; callers can set status to any string including invalid lifecycle values.
findings.fix: Replace status: String with TelemetryStatus enum (Pending, Validated, Sent). mark_sent should return TelemetryWorkflow with the Sent variant, not mutate a string.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are independent lifecycle booleans that can be set in any combination independently of status, allowing invalid state combinations like is_validated=true, is_sent=true, status="pending".
findings.failure_mode: Booleans are set separately from status, so no invariant is enforced at the type level. A caller can set is_validated=true without ever validating, or set is_sent=true without updating status, producing logically inconsistent telemetry records.
findings.fix: Fold lifecycle booleans into the typestate enum variants. Validated variant carries validation metadata; Sent variant carries send timestamp. No separate bool fields needed.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is a top-level optional field that can be Some(timestamp) while is_sent=false and status is not "sent". This creates invalid states where telemetry appears sent without being sent.
findings.failure_mode: Downstream code checking sent_at_epoch_ms.is_some() may treat the telemetry as sent even when is_sent=false and status is not "sent". The Option is decoupled from the lifecycle invariant it should belong to.
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the typestate enum's Sent variant (e.g., Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }). The Option is eliminated because the variant itself encodes presence/absence of send data.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive that allows empty strings, duplicate IDs, malformed UUIDs, or any arbitrary string. No newtype wrapper enforces ID invariants.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can create TelemetryWorkflow with id="", id="null", or duplicate IDs. No validation at construction. String methods like .len() or .is_empty() leak into domain logic instead of being encapsulated.
findings.fix: Define a TelemetryId newtype (e.g., pub struct TelemetryId(String)) with a smart constructor that validates non-empty format. Use TelemetryId in TelemetryWorkflow instead of raw String.

findings.problem: mark_sent accepts TelemetryWorkflow with raw String fields and mutable fields directly. There is no parse boundary: raw primitives cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors, so callers can construct invalid domain states directly by mutating item.status = "sent".to_string() and item.is_sent = true without any validation.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller with a TelemetryWorkflow reference can mutate status and is_sent independently of each other and without validation, bypassing all lifecycle invariants. No smart constructor validates that is_validated was true before marking sent, no error return for pre-condition violations.
findings.fix: Replace mark_sent with a fallible smart constructor: fn try_mark_sent(item: TelemetryWorkflow) -> Result<TelemetryWorkflow, TelemetryError>. Validate preconditions (status must be Validated, not already Sent) before transitioning. Make fields non-public and provide only constructor methods.

findings.problem: All fields (id, status, is_validated, is_sent, sent_at_epoch_ms) are pub, allowing external mutation without any validation or encapsulation. This defeats all invariants.
findings.failure_mode: External code can do item.is_validated = false after validation, or item.is_sent = true without updating status, with no way to detect or prevent the mutation.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide constructors and state-transition methods that enforce invariants. Use a typestate enum for lifecycle transitions.

residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate compiles but permits all illegal telemetry states at compile time because lifecycle is modeled as independent String/bool/Option fields instead of a typestate enum. No tests, no benchmarks, no error taxonomy, no smart constructors, no field encapsulation. All absolute-law violations in this review (no unsafe/unwrap/panic present) are offset by the fundamental type-system failure: illegal states are fully representable and mutable.
